You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H0989

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "to cease, stop; (Pa'el) to cause to cease, make stop -- used of halting work or activity by decree"
  Readable gloss: "An Aramaic verb found exclusively in Ezra, describing the stopping of construction on the Jerusalem temple. In its basic Pe'al stem it means simply 'to cease' or 'to stop,' as when the rebuilding work ground to a halt (Ezra 4:24). In the causative Pa'el stem, it describes the forcible halting of work by hostile officials who compelled the Jews to stop building. Spanish renders both stems distinctly -- 'cesar' for the intransitive and 'hacer cesar' for the causative -- preserving the voice distinction clearly."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "cause to cease, make stop (causative)"
    Enriched: The causative Pa'el stem (equivalent to the Hebrew Piel), meaning to force an activity to stop by external authority or decree. All four occurrences involve political opponents compelling the cessation of temple rebuilding (Ezra 4:21, 23; 5:5; 6:8). Spanish 'hicieron cesar' and English 'stopped/caused to cease' consistently mark the agent who enforces the halt.
    Existing Spanish translations: hicieron-cesar, para-hacer-cesar, sean-detenidos, y-los-hicieron-cesar
  Sense 2: "cease, stop (intransitive)"
    Enriched: The intransitive Pe'al stem (equivalent to the Hebrew Qal), meaning to come to a stop on its own or as a result of prior action. Both occurrences appear in Ezra 4:24 -- the perfect and participle forms -- describing the temple work that had ceased. Spanish 'cesada/ceso' and English 'stopped' capture the stative, resultative quality of work that simply was no longer happening.
    Existing Spanish translations: cesada, cesó
